subtasks.title: Ayurveda history and philosophy
subtasks.instructions: Find reputable sources on the history, origins, and core philosophical principles of Ayurveda (e.g., the three doshas, the concept of Prakriti). Quote each fact with its source.

subtasks.title: Ayurveda practices and modern relevance
subtasks.instructions: Find reputable sources on common Ayurvedic practices (herbal remedies, diet, yoga, Panchakarma) and any modern scientific research or recognition of Ayurveda. Quote each fact with its source.

findings.title: Historical origins in Vedic/Buddhist texts
findings.detail: Ayurvedic terminology and concepts appear in the Buddhist Canon from the middle of the first millennium BCE onwards.

evidence.quote: Historical evidence for Ayurvedic terminology and concepts appear in the Buddhist Canon from the middle of the first millennium BCE onwards.

findings.title: Classical texts dated to first centuries CE
findings.detail: The main classical Ayurveda texts are datable in their present form to the first centuries CE, beginning with accounts of knowledge transmission from gods to sages.

evidence.quote: The main classical Ayurveda texts are datable in their present form to the first centuries CE.

findings.title: Core Ayurvedic therapies
findings.detail: Ayurveda therapies include herbal medicines, special diets, meditation, yoga, massage, laxatives, enemas, and medical oils.

evidence.quote: Therapies include herbal medicines , special diets , meditation , yoga , massage , laxatives , enemas , and medical oils.

findings.title: Panchakarma detoxification
findings.detail: Panchakarma are techniques to eliminate toxic elements from the body, performed in sequence to restore balance through purgation.

evidence.quote: According to Ayurveda, panchakarma are techniques to eliminate toxic elements from the body .
